subject: Multigroup analysis - setting some of the same coefficient to zero and others to be freely estimated

messages.author: 08e48595b188026f
messages.subject: Multigroup analysis - setting some of the same coefficient to zero and others to be freely estimated
parts:
Hi,

I'm doing multigroup analysis with 3 groups and I want to constrain the effect of one variable to be zero in two groups and freely estimated in the third group.

Example syntax 1:
var1~ var2 + var3
var4 ~ var1 + c(x,0,0)*var2

But in this case, it sets the effect of var2 on var4 to "x" in all groups.

Example syntax 2:
var1~ var2 + var3
var4 ~ var1 + c(0.1,0,0)*var2

In this case it sets the effect of var2 on var 4 to 0.1 in all groups and outputs the warning "lavaan WARNING: equality constraints involve fixed parameters with different values; only the first one will be used"

Is there any way to make this work? I do not understand why the warning as it works fine if I set c(a,b,c)*var2 ...

Thanks for any help!
Jošt

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: Multigroup analysis - setting some of the same coefficient to zero and others to be freely estimated
parts:
Jost,
Try this.

require(lavaan)
model <- '
var1~ var2 + var3
var4 ~ var1 + c(NA,0,0)*var2
'
lavaanify(model, ngroups=3)

Keith

messages.subject: Re: Multigroup analysis - setting some of the same coefficient to zero and others to be freely estimated
parts:
Dear Keith,

thank you for this suggestion. 'lavaanify' returns a specification that is correct (estimate for var2 is set to free in group but constraint to zero in other two groups). However, when passing this to the sem function it still constraints parameters for this variable to zero in all three groups.

I found a workaround, but it includes more manual work. My command for evaluation of the (path) model was:

mga.path.con<- sem(model = myModel, data = myData, estimator = "MLR",
                     missing = "FIML", fixed.x = F,
                     group = "myGroup", group.equal = "regressions")

When I remove the argument ' group.equal = "regressions" ' and manually constrain all the parameters I want to be equal, also this part (i.e., c(NA, 0, 0)*var2) works fine.

Maybe there is an issue between the two commands? (i.e., group.equal = "regressions" and c(NA, 0, 0)*var2 )
Also, I wonder how one would proceed if there were four (or more) groups, and would want to constrain the parameters in two groups to equal but in the other two to zero. Not my issue at the moment, but just wondering.

Regards,
Jošt

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: Multigroup analysis - setting some of the same coefficient to zero and others to be freely estimated
parts:
Jost,
Anticipating which of two conflicting instructions will take precedence comes with experience.  In this case, yes, your group.equal parameter took precedence over your model syntax.  (I got tripped up over a similar precedence issue learning to use Blackboard Advanced Adaptive Release feature.)

Here is an example with four groups as you described.  The constraint is imposed by using the same label in this case but you can also impose it directly in cases where this will not work for you.  (Note that using different labels for groups 3 and 4 would amount to the same thing because 0 = 0.)

var4 ~ var1 + c(a,a,b,b)*var2 + c(NA,NA,0,0)*var2
'
lavaanify(model, ngroups=4)

You can use the above script paradigm to test out other variations.

Sources: lavaan options help file, model.syntax help file, online tutorial model syntax pages.
